issues.problem: Bracketed interpretation '(मादाओं)' (females) is not in the text and is forbidden inside translations; English has no such addition.

The flag calls the printed ṝ a 'probable typo' with a firm suggestion. The Vedic samhitā convention (r dropped before r-initial, with compensatory lengthening) can produce exactly this printed form, so it is at least as likely to be regular printing as an error. Soften to 'unusual; possibly regular Vedic sandhi, not certainly a typo'. No patch (text_flags not patchable).
issues.fix: soften why: 'unusual ṝ (probably the printed Vedic r-sandhi pṛṣatībhir ṛṣṭibhiḥ); check the edition'

issues.problem: 'प्रेरित' means 'impelled/sent'; English and gloss say 'inspired one' (vipra), a different sense. Use a plain Hindi transliteration of the word to avoid a wrong sense.
'prati' is glossed 'toward' but is dropped in both translations. Acceptable as a preverb idiom, but say so in notes.

patch.text: prati vīhi: prati is a preverb with vīhi ('partake'); not rendered separately.

issues.problem: Hindi takes tṛpat as a participle ('satisfied') while English and gloss take it as adverb 'to satisfaction'; align with the gloss.
पुरुषार्थ is a loaded later technical term (the four aims); nṛmṇa = manly power.

'Brāhmaṇa priest' conflicts with the glossary pair Brahman priest (m., ब्रह्मा) vs brahman (n.); here the word is brāhmaṇa (m.). The identification of the office is not stated in the line. Needs a glossary decision (e.g. 'from the Brāhmaṇa'); the note should say the exact office is unclear.
Gender 'm.' is asserted for a form the notes call uncertain; the stem (āvṛta / āvṛt) is not settled.
